title: Supervisor decides every scheduled fire of a flow
description: Connect the Supervisor to the scheduler. fwd's default onFire asks the Supervisor about every fire of a stream whose key names a flow shipped under flows/. The fire is admitted only when the Supervisor would let that flow run now; the fire itself makes the flow due, so not_due never holds it. Otherwise the fire is recorded as held, and its reason starts with the gate that holds it (for example "flow_disabled: The Owner has not turned this flow on."). Streams that are not flows are decided as before. A failure while deciding holds the fire, as the scheduler already does. Admitting a fire only records it as fired: starting the flow's cycle from a fired stream, and handing finished items to a sending app, are later rows. Nothing here changes a gate, a cap, the dial or the core policy.
acceptance: A fire of a flow that the Owner has not enabled is recorded as held, and its reason starts with flow_disabled
Once the Owner enables the flow, its fire is recorded as fired, not held by not_due

A paused Supervisor, an Autopilot flow whose channels changed since the Owner confirmed, a flow whose logic fails, and the kill switch each hold the fire, and the reason names supervisor_paused, dial_unapproved, no_engine or kill_switch
A fire of a stream that is not a flow is still fired
fwd uses the Supervisor as its scheduler's onFire by default
